Rashi on Sotah 2b:10:1.hebrew: בה - בטומאה קאי, דהא מינה סליק: "והיא נטמאה", "ועד אין בה". ודרשינן: אין בה תרי, אלא חד:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:10:1.english: In her - It refers to the defilement, for the passage ascends from it: "and she was defiled," "and there is no witness against her [lit. in her]." And we expound: [if] there are not two [witnesses] in her, but [there is] one [witness, she is still forbidden].

Rashi on Sotah 2b:10:2.hebrew: בה - עד אחד נאמן, ולא בקינוי:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:10:2.english: "In her" - A single witness is believed, but not with regard to jealousy [warning].

Rashi on Sotah 2b:14:1.english: Seclusion is preferable - To treat her more stringently.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:14:2.hebrew: שכן אוסרתה - על הבעל ועל הבועל מספק:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:14:2.english: For it prohibits her - to the husband and to the paramour, due to uncertainty.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:14:3.hebrew: כטומאה - ודאית, כדדרשינן לקמן: מגיד לך הכתוב שעל הספק אסורה, בפרק כשם שהמים בודקין (דף כח.):
Rashi on Sotah 2b:14:3.english: Like impurity - [Meaning,] definite [impurity], as we expound below: "The verse tells you that she is forbidden [to her husband] even on account of a doubt," in the chapter "Just as the water tests" (28a).

Rashi on Sotah 2b:15:1.hebrew: שכן עיקר גרם לה - שע"י הקינוי סתירתה אוסרתה:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:15:1.english: For it is the primary cause for her - For through the warning, her seclusion renders her forbidden [to her husband].

Rashi on Sotah 2b:18:1.hebrew: מתני' - דקתני לר"א דקינוי בשנים, וסתירה על פי עצמו:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:18:1.english: Our Mishnah - For it teaches, according to Rabbi Eliezer, that the warning [is given] before two [witnesses], and the seclusion [is established] on the basis of [the husband] himself.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:18:2.hebrew: דלא כי האי תנא - דקתני לר"א: סתירה בשנים, וקינוי על פי עצמו:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:18:2.english: [Our Mishnah] is not like this Tanna - For [our Mishnah] teaches, according to R. Eliezer, that [the woman's] seclusion [requires] two [witnesses], and the warning [may be given] on the husband's own word.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:1:1.hebrew: ממשמע שנאמר עד - ולא נאמר "עדים", איני יודע דאחד קאמר. אלא מדאיצטריך למיכתב "אחד", שמע מינה דעד שנים משמע, דאינו אלא לשון עדות, וסתם עדות — שנים:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:1:1.english: From the implication of the fact that it says "a witness" - and it does not say "witnesses," I would not know that it means one. Rather, from the fact that it needed to write "one," learn from this that "a witness" implies two, for it is nothing other than a term of testimony, and unspecified testimony [requires] two.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:22:1.hebrew: לדברי ר"י בר' יהודה אין לדברי ר' אליעזר סוף - ולקמן מפרש לה:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:22:1.english: According to the words of R. Yosei son of R. Yehudah, there is no end to the words of R. Eliezer - And below, [the Gemara] explains it.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:22:2.hebrew: מאי ניהו - אין לדבר סוף, דקאמר:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:22:2.english: What is it? - [What is the meaning of] "the matter has no end," which [Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda] said?

Rashi on Sotah 2b:22:3.hebrew: ואמר קנאי - כשכועס עליה, אומר: ״קנאתי לה מפלוני״, ומביא עדים שנסתרה עמו סתירה כל שהוא. דכיון דלא קינא לה, לא נזהרה בו:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:22:3.english: And he said, "I warned her" - When he is angry at her, he says, "I warned her about so-and-so," and brings witnesses that she secluded herself with him, even for a minimal [period of] seclusion. For since he did not [actually] warn her, she was not careful with him.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:23:1.hebrew: הא למשנתינו יש סוף - לדברי רבי אליעזר, בתמיה:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:23:1.english: But according to our Mishnah, does the matter have an end? - According to the words of Rabbi Eliezer, [this is said] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:23:2.hebrew: והא זמנין דלא איסתתר - ואומר "ראיתיה שנסתרה":
Rashi on Sotah 2b:23:2.english: But sometimes she did not seclude herself - and [the witness] says, "I saw that she secluded herself."

Rashi on Sotah 2b:25:1.english: And it is not necessary [to say] regarding our Mishna - [This is said] as an expression of astonishment (i.e., as a rhetorical question).

Rashi on Sotah 2b:25:2.hebrew: איכא עיקר - שכבר התחיל בעדים שלא ע"י כעס:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:25:2.english: There is a main [part] - For [the matter] has already begun with witnesses, not through anger.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:25:3.hebrew: הכא ליכא עיקר - ולכשיכעוס נקל לומר "קנאתי", והוא ימצא לה סתירות הרבה:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:25:3.english: Here there is no principal [basis] - And when he becomes angry, it is easy to say, "I warned [her]," and he will find many [instances of] seclusion for her.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:27:1.hebrew: לא לימא איניש - אפילו בינו לבינה:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:27:1.english: A person should not say - Even between him and her [i.e., privately].

Rashi on Sotah 2b:27:2.english: And she is secluded - And she becomes secluded, and becomes forbidden to him.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:28:1.hebrew: קנאה - כעס, כמו "הם קנאוני בלא אל" (דברים ל״ב:כ״א), "כי קנאה חמת גבר" (משלי ו׳:ל״ד):
Rashi on Sotah 2b:28:1.english: Jealousy (kinah) - Anger, as in "They have provoked Me to jealousy with a non-god" (Deuteronomy 32:21), and "For jealousy is the fury of a man" (Proverbs 6:34).

Rashi on Sotah 2b:28:2.hebrew: מאי דקמא - מה יש לפנינו? מה אירע עכשיו, שזו בודלת מן האנשים:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:28:2.english: What [is] the matter before us - What do we have before us? What happened now, that this one separates herself from the men?

Rashi on Sotah 2b:29:1.hebrew: וכולי עלמא ידעי דקני לה - שהעדים מגלין הדבר, ואינן שונאין אותה:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:29:1.english: And everyone knows that he warned her - For the witnesses reveal the matter, and they do not hate her.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:29:2.english: And he who comes to make a warning [of jealousy] with her - For she provokes him, because he suspects her.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:2:1.hebrew: ואמר רחמנא תרי לית בה - לעיל קאי, לפרושי מסקנא דמילתיה: היכי מידריש "ועד אין בה":
Rashi on Sotah 2b:2:1.english: And the Merciful One said: [Where there are] two, there is not in it - This stands above [i.e., refers back to the earlier statement], to explain the conclusion of his statement: how the verse "and there is no witness against her" is expounded.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:3:1.hebrew: אלא טעמא כו' - קושיא היא. כלומר: טעמא דכתיב "לא יקום עד אחד" — דההוא מוכח לך דהאי "ועד אין בה" בתרי קאמר; הא לאו הכי, הוה אמינא: עד דכתיב הכא בסוטה חד הוא, וקאמרינן: אפילו אחד אין בה:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:3:1.english: Rather, the reason, etc. - It is a question. That is to say: [Is] the reason [that it is not enough for her to be defiled by one witness] that it is written, "One witness shall not rise" — for that [verse] proves to you that this [phrase] "and there is no witness against her" speaks of two [witnesses]? Were it not so, I would have said: the "witness" written here regarding a sotah is one, and we would be saying that even one [witness] is not [to be found] against her.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:4:1.hebrew: איצטריך - "לא יקום עד אחד" לגלויי עליה דהאי, ולאשמעינן דחד מהימן. דאי לאו הכי, הוה אמינא: כל סתם "עד" אחד הוא, ובסוטה לא הוה אמינא דמיתסרא, ואפי' בעד א', וכל שכן בלא עד. והכי הוה דרשינן ליה: "ועד אין בה" דקא אמר רחמנא, הכי קאמר: ועד אחד אין נאמן בה, אלא שנים:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:4:1.english: It was necessary - [The verse] "One witness shall not rise" [was needed] to reveal this matter about her, and to teach us that one [witness] is believed. For if not so, I would have said: Every unspecified "witness" is [only] one, and in the case of a sota I would not have said that she becomes forbidden [to her husband] even through one witness, and certainly not without a witness. And this is how we would have expounded it: "And there is no witness against her," which the Merciful One said, it means this: And one witness is not believed against her, only two.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:5:1.english: And we object: [Is it that] he is not believed regarding her? - [This is stated] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:5:2.hebrew: אלא מאי בעי - קרא "עד דאיכא תרי", בתמיה? אמאי אתא קרא להאי? לשתוק קרא מיניה כו':
Rashi on Sotah 2b:5:2.english: Rather, what does it want - [Does] the verse [mean] "until there are two," [asked] incredulously? Why did the verse come [to teach] this? Let the verse be silent about it, etc.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:6:1.hebrew: דבר דבר מממון - כתיב בנואפת כי מצא בה ערות דבר (דברים כ״ד:א׳), וכתיב בדיני ממונות ע"פ שני עדים יקום דבר (שם יט):
Rashi on Sotah 2b:6:1.english: [Derive] "matter" [from] "matter" from monetary law - It is written regarding the adulteress, "for he has found in her some unseemly matter [ervat davar]" (Deuteronomy 24:1), and it is written regarding monetary cases, "on the testimony of two witnesses a matter shall be established" (ibid. 19).

Rashi on Sotah 2b:7:1.hebrew: איצטריך - "לא יקום" לגלויי עליה דהאי "עד", דבשנים הכתוב מדבר. דאי לא גלי עליה, הוה אמינא "עד" חד משמע, ואין נאמן בה קאתא קרא לאשמועינן. ודקשיא לך למה לי קרא — סלקא דעתך אמינא: סוטה שאחר קינוי וסתירה, בא עד אחד והעיד שנטמאה באותה סתירה — שאני, וראוי להאמינו כאן, שהרי רגלים לדבר:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:7:1.english: It was necessary - "[A witness] shall not rise" [was needed] to reveal about this "witness" that the verse speaks of two. For if it had not been revealed about him, I would have said that "witness" implies one, and the verse would have come to teach us that he is not believed in her case. And as for your difficulty — why do I need a verse [at all]? It might have entered your mind to say: A sotah, where after the warning and the seclusion one witness came and testified that she was defiled in that seclusion, is different, and it is proper to believe him here, since there are circumstantial grounds for the matter.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:8:1.hebrew: ומי מצית אמרת - דאי לא גלי רחמנא דכל עד שנים הם, דאנא אמינא דהאי "עד אין בה" — "אין נאמן בה" קאמר, א"כ בא הכתוב להקל עליה:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:8:1.english: And can you say - For if the Merciful One had not revealed that every [kind of] witness means two, I would say that this [phrase] "there is no witness against her" means "a single witness is not believed against her." If so, the verse came to be lenient toward her.

Rashi on Sotah 2b:8:2.hebrew: והא מדכתיב והיא לא נתפשה מכלל - דפשיטא לך דנטמאה. והיכי קאמר "והיא לא נתפשה" אועד אין בה? נהי דרישא דקרא איכא למימר ע"י שנים עדים ושכב איש אותה בעדים, ועד אחד אין נאמן בה, אלא "והיא לא נתפשה" היכי קאי אאין נאמן בה? הא אמרת דלא מחזקי לה בנבעלת:
Rashi on Sotah 2b:8:2.english: But from the fact that it is written "and she was not taken," [it follows] - that it is obvious to you that she was defiled. And how does it say "and she was not taken" with regard to "there is no witness against her"? Granted, regarding the first part of the verse, one can say [that it refers to a case] through two witnesses — "and a man lay with her" — with witnesses, and a single witness is not believed against her; but how does "and she was not taken" apply to [the case of] "he is not believed against her"? Surely you said that we do not presume her to have been had relations with.

Tosafot on Sotah 2b:10:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא דר' יהושע - בירושלמי מפיק ליה מהני קראי: מאי טעמא דרבי יהושע? "כי מצא בה ערות דבר" — "ערוה" זו הסתירה, "דבר" זו הקינוי. וילפינן "דבר דבר": מה דבר האמור להלן על פי שנים, אף כאן ע"פ שנים. תני רבי יוסי בר' יהודה וכו': משקה ע"פ שנים נאמר "כי מצא", ואין מציאה בכל מקום אלא על פי עדים. מה מקיים רבי אליעזר "דבר דבר"? שהוא מרגיל לבא לידי ערוה. עוד בירושלמי: כתיב "ועבר עליו רוח קנאה" וגו', שלא יקנא לה מתוך שחוק, ולא מתוך קלות ראש, ולא מתוך גאות, אלא מתוך דבר של אימה. עבר וקינא לה מחמת הדברים הללו, מה את אמרת: למצוה או לעיכוב? אם תאמר למצוה — קינויו קינוי; אם תאמר לעיכוב — אין קינויו קינוי. אמר רבי מנא: אתיא כהדא, כל מקום שנאמר "חוקה" — תורה מעכב:
Tosafot on Sotah 2b:10:1.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehoshua - In the Yerushalmi, [the Gemara] derives it from these verses: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehoshua? "For he found in her an *ervat davar*" — "*ervah*" is the *seterah* (seclusion), and "*davar*" is the warning. And we derive it by [the analogy of] "*davar*, *davar*": Just as the "*davar*" stated elsewhere [requires testimony] by two witnesses, so too here [it requires] two witnesses. It was taught: Rabbi Yosei the son of Rabbi Yehudah, etc.: [As for] the one who gives her to drink, "for he found" is said [to require testimony] by two witnesses, and "finding" is always only through witnesses. What, then, does Rabbi Eliezer do with "*davar*, *davar*"? [He explains] that it is something that habitually leads to *ervah*. Further in the Yerushalmi: It is written, "and a spirit of jealousy passes over him," etc. — that he should not warn her out of levity, nor out of frivolity, nor out of arrogance, but out of a matter of awe. If he transgressed and warned her on account of these things, what do you say: is it a *mitzvah* [only] or is it a requirement [for validity]? If you say it is a *mitzvah*, his warning is a [valid] warning; if you say it is a requirement, his warning is not a warning. Rabbi Mana said: It follows from this: Anywhere that "*chukah*" is stated, the Torah makes it a requirement.

Tosafot on Sotah 2b:1:1.hebrew: כל מקום שנאמר עד הרי כאן שנים - ואחד, דכתיב גבי "ועד אחד לא יענה בנפש" (במדבר לה), מוקי לה בפרק אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לד.) בדרישה מן התלמידים. ו"לא יומת על פי עד אחד" (דברים יז) דרשינן בפרק ראשון דמכות (דף ו:) לעדות מיוחדת, לאפוקי אחד רואה מחלון זה ואחד רואה מחלון זה. אבל קשיא: דגבי שבועת העדות כתיב "והוא עד" (ויקרא ה), ומחייבין אפילו אחד, כדתנן (שבועות דף לא:): "כפר אחד והודה אחד, הכופר חייב". וי"ל: דשבועת העדות לא חייבה תורה אלא בתביעה, כדילפינן התם מקראי; הילכך כל היכא דמפסידו ממון מיחייב, דבהפסד ממון תליא מילתא:
Tosafot on Sotah 2b:1:1.english: Wherever it says "witness," there are at least two here - And as for the one [witness], regarding which it is written, "and one witness shall not testify against a person to die" (Numbers 35), [the Gemara] establishes it in the chapter "Echad Dinei Mamonot" (Sanhedrin 34a) as referring to the cross-examination of the students. And "a person shall not be put to death on the testimony of one witness" (Deuteronomy 17) we expound in the first chapter of Makkot (6b) as referring to a "unique testimony," to exclude [a case where] one [witness] sees from this window and one sees from that window. But there is a difficulty: for regarding the oath of testimony it is written, "and he is a witness" (Leviticus 5), and we obligate even a single [witness], as we learned (Shevuot 31b): "One [person] denied and one [witness] admitted [that he had testimony] — the one who denied is liable." And one can answer: that the Torah obligated the oath of testimony only where there is a claim [by the plaintiff], as we derive there from the verses; therefore, whenever [the witness's denial] causes [the plaintiff] to lose money, he is liable, for the matter depends on monetary loss.
